ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, general partners, authorized signatories, and any person holding 25% or more of the partnership's capital against: the domestic Canadian Consolidated Sanctions List (under Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act); the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; and PEP databases (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv World-Check) for politically exposed persons and high-risk control relationships. The licensed corporate service provider or law firm acting as formation agent is a reporting entity under the PCMLTFA and must complete identity verification, maintain a beneficial-ownership record, and perform continuous transaction monitoring; enhanced due diligence is triggered by any PEP, sanctions match, negative media, or elevated risk indicator. Screening evidence and risk assessments must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship terminates, in accordance with FINTRAC record-keeping and compliance requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises en ligne (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, the registered name of a Quebec limited partnership must be expressed in French or contain a French-language version; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. When an English designation is desired, it may appear only accompanied by a French designation. The statutory legal suffix for a Quebec limited partnership is 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.'; in bilingual usage, 'limited partnership' or 'L.P.' may be used as the secondary designation. A registered trademark exemption may apply only if the name is protected as a trademark under the federal Trademarks Act and is used concurrently in a French context.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Assurance / Insurance / Underwriting: requires prior authorization from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) and must not imply that the partnership itself is an insurer or underwriter
Banque / Bank / Trust / Fiducie / Caisses: prohibited without a charter under the Bank Act (Canada) or federal/Quebec trust-company statutes
Avocat / Notaire / Notary / CPA / Comptable professionnel agréé / Ingénieur / Architecte: prohibited unless the named professional is a member of the applicable professional order
Université / Collège / École / Institut / Hôpital: restricted or prohibited without ministerial or statutory authorization
Royal / Impériale / Gouvernement / Canada / Québec / Montréal / Société d'État: requires prior ministerial consent or is absolutely reserved
Corporation / Inc. / Ltd / Limitée / Société par actions: misleading for a limited partnership and prohibited as the principal legal suffix, except where expressly required by other rules
Names implying immorality, falsehood, or an intention to defraud: prohibited on public-order grounds under the legal publicity statute
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name-refusal notice from the Registraire des entreprises, the applicant or its legal representative may file a written administrative review request within 30 days of the refusal with the Director of Enterprise Registration, attaching revised naming options, a legal justification under CQLR c. P-44.1 and the Charter of the French Language, and any authorization documents for restricted tokens. If the refusal is confirmed, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec within 60 days of confirmation under articles 529 and 846 of the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c. C-25.01. A name reservation may be renewed or a new application filed before expiry, provided the original name has not become unavailable due to a conflicting third-party reservation or registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable with conditions. The Registraire des entreprises requires a physical postal address in Quebec and a chief establishment where corporate and accounting records are kept; a post-office box alone is impermissible. A licensed commercial virtual-office or service-agent address located in Quebec is accepted for a low-risk professional marine surveying partnership if the agent accepts service of process, is physically occupied, and maintains normal business hours. Because the entity will conduct marine survey and claims inspection rather than selling or underwriting insurance, no additional financial-sector occupancy mandate applies; however, Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency will expect documented operational substance, so a home-office declaration, sublease, or mobile field-base arrangement should be evidenced in the partnership's books and record-keeping system.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 8% aggregate estimated probability of an unannounced on-site verification within any 12-month period by the Registraire des entreprises, Revenu Québec, or the Canada Revenue Agency. Unannounced inspections are more likely if UBO declarations are incomplete, nominee structures are detected, or GST/QST and corporate-tax filings diverge from stated commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CCQ) arts. 2236-2265 (limited partnership); Act respecting the registration of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons, CQLR c. A-3.001, ss. 24-54; Act respecting the conduct of business of partnerships, CQLR c. P-6, ss. 1-17
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation pour société en commandite (Declaration of Registration for Limited Partnership) – Form A or electronic equivalent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; partners must subscribe and contribute the amounts set out in the partnership agreement. No escrow account is required under Quebec law. Limited partners may withdraw profits subject to art. 2251 CCQ, but a return of capital does not reduce their liability unless it renders an estate insolvent under art. 2259 CCQ.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner, acting for and on behalf of the Initial Limited Partners, hereby: (1) adopts the Partnership Agreement of ___ LP and accepts the subscriptions, contributions and capital commitments in the signature pages, without any escrow requirement; (2) establishes the registered office at the address in the Declaration of Registration and designates the Registraire des entreprises as official recipient of notices; (3) appoints ___ and ___ as managing general partner and secretary-treasurer, with authority to open bank accounts and pay incorporation fees; and (4) authorizes the filing of the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises and ancillary registrations with Revenu Québec. All actions previously taken by organizers are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online name analysis and reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name clearance application providing a proposed trade name in French or bilingual, and a short non-technical description of the marine hull and cargo damage survey activity. Pay the name analysis fee (approx. CAD $25). The Registrar will issue a name reservation valid for 90 days upon approval.
required_dossiers: Proposed name and keywords for the name analysis request
Short description of the main business purpose
Consent of any individual whose name is used in the partnership name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused, file a modified name request or submit a written application for administrative review within 15 days; a rejection may be appealed to the Court of Quebec under ARSP ss. 22-26.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Partnership Agreement and Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal advisor / notary; preparation only, no filing with the Registrar yet
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement and the Déclaration d'immatriculation for a société en commandite. The declaration must state the partnership name, the registered office street address in Quebec, the full names and addresses of every general partner, the aggregate amount and nature of limited partners' contributions, and a statement that limited partners do not participate in management. Execute the declaration before a notary if necessary, and have each general partner sign the agreement.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement (acte de société)
Déclaration d'immatriculation (signed by all general partners)
Schedule of limited partners' contributions and capital commitments
Power of attorney appointing a Quebec service representative, if any general partner is non-resident
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration fails to designate a Canadian resident general partner or a service representative for non-residents, the registrar will require correction; cure by filing a corrective declaration within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission and Payment of Filing Fees to the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Secure electronic filings portal (compte d'usager)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enter the declaration data in the online filing form, attach the signed PDF counterpart, and submit the payment of CAD $85 (approx. US$63) by credit card or wire. After validation of mandatory fields, the Registrar will issue a recording acknowledgement and assign the Numéro d'Entreprise du Québec (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Completed and signed electronic declaration of registration
Payment receipt for the filing fee
If a non-resident general partner is involved, the power of attorney appointing a service representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an Avis de rejet for missing or inconsistent data, correct and resubmit within 30 days to preserve the priority filing date; a later resubmission requires an additional filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Registration Certificate and Official Registry Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Certificate issuance and public registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Certificat d'immatriculation once the declaration is posted in the public registry. Verify that the registered office, general partners and partnership name appear accurately. Obtain the Statement of Information and certified copies from the registrar for banking, contractual and licensing purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration (electronically issued)
Statement of information from the public registry
NEQ confirmation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Clerical errors in the certificate may be rectified by filing Form F (correction) with the Registrar, supported by copies of the originally filed declaration; false information may be sanctioned under ARSP s. 60.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax and Occupational Safety Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (RQ), Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the NEQ and any federal Business Number to register for GST/HST, Québec QST, and employer accounts if the partnership has employees. If the partnership will employ personnel, open a CNESST file and obtain a workplace classification for marine surveying. Register for the Revenu Québec partnership information return (TP-600) at the end of the fiscal period.
required_dossiers: NEQ and partnership registration certificate
Partnership agreement and identification of all partners
Employer payroll information if applicable
Detailed business activity description for CNESST classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration may trigger a penalty; submit a voluntary disclosure or Notice of Objection within 30 days and provide the missing factual information to obtain a waiver of penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner and partners (internal governance); no governmental filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt by unanimous written consent the first governance resolution covering: appointment of the managing general partner; approval of the partnership agreement; opening of Canadian bank accounts with dual signature authority; adoption of the fiscal year and annual reporting calendar; and appointment of the external accountant and bookkeeper for filing partnership returns.
required_dossiers: Unanimous written consent or minutes of first meeting
List of authorized bank signatories
Minute book containing the partnership agreement and register of limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the general partners are deadlocked, the default management rules in CCQ arts. 2251-2252 apply; a partner may apply to the Superior Court of Quebec for a protective order or dissolution in serious cases.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) – Direction de l'expertise et de la distribution de l'assurance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence d'expert en sinistre (claims adjuster licence) – maritime hull and cargo class, issued under the Act respecting the distribution of financial products and services (CQLR c. D-9.2), Part V, ss. 240 and 246; the firm must also be registered as an adjusting firm with the AMF

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt – professional and field survey operations with no industrial discharge or emission source; no certificate of authorization required for the office or marine survey activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC emissions from the surveying operations; compliance with municipal sewer by-laws for office use, with the Québec Contaminated Sites Regulation (CQLR c. Q-2) for any handling of contaminated cargo or fuel samples, and with the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 for vessel inspection so that no marine pollution occurs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain a certificat de sécurité incendie from the municipal fire prevention service for the registered office. Structural: provide the building occupancy certificate (CO) for the office; for field work at ports, obtain the port authority's wharf pass and safety clearance. Occupational: register with CNESST, obtain a first-aid assessment and compliance certificate, and maintain a health and safety file in accordance with Quebec OHS legislation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal GST/HST: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Number Registry and My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). Quebec QST: Revenu Quebec, Services en ligne des entreprises / My Quebec portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca). Prerequisite non-tax registry: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ), which issues the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and transmits the data to Revenu Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Register the CA_LP with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec to obtain the NEQ; provide the limited partnership agreement, registered office address in Quebec, and for each overseas partner the foreign registration or tax identification number. STEP 2: Open the federal account with CRA using Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1, identifying the partnership itself as the GST/HST registrant; CRA issues a 9-digit Business Number (BN) with an RT program account. STEP 3: Complete QST registration with Revenu Quebec, either directly in the linked online portal or on Form LM-1/V, after the NEQ and BN accounts exist; Revenu Quebec issues a distinct QST registration number. STEP 4: Where all partners are non-residents, appoint a Canadian representative for service and maintain a Canadian postal address; CRA may require security for current or future GST/HST liabilities. The LP remains voluntarily registrable before the threshold is crossed, which is advisable to recover Quebec input tax refunds on survey instruments, subcontracted inspectors, and marine-transport expenses.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. For income tax the CA_LP is fiscally transparent under Income Tax Act s.96 and the Quebec Taxation Act; partners, not the partnership, report allocable Canadian-source business income, and non-resident partners are exposed to Canadian income tax only to the extent the LP carries on business through a permanent establishment in Canada. For GST/QST purposes, however, the partnership is a distinct person and registrant in its own name: the CA_LP invoices marine survey fees, charges GST and QST, and claims input tax credits, while the general partner, as counterparty of record, remains responsible for the partnership's tax obligations in liquidation and assessment proceedings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; a Quebec LP is transparent by force of law. Relevant elections include: (i) a fiscal-period election under ITA s.249.1 to align the partnership taxation year with the partner inclusion rules; (ii) the GST/HST Quick Method election and annual-basis remittance election for eligible small registrants; (iii) an election to align the QST reporting period with the GST/HST reporting period for submission to Revenu Quebec; and (iv) an election by the LP to waive the zero-rating of export supplies where the documentary burden is disproportionate to the tax saving. The 2021 Canadian hybrid-mismatch regime (ITA ss.18.6-18.7 and the parallel QSTA provisions) operates automatically as a mandatory denial/inclusion rule without elective carve-outs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal goods and services tax) administered by CRA, combined with Quebec Sales Tax (QST) administered by Revenu Quebec; Quebec is not an HST harmonized province, so the two taxes are charged separately but on the same taxable supply of marine surveying services performed in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 Canadian dollars of worldwide taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies, in any single calendar quarter or in the trailing four consecutive calendar quarters; the identical small-supplier threshold applies to both GST/HST and QST. A foreign marine insurance surveyor physically performing inspections at Quebec ports or on vessels in Quebec territorial waters will normally exceed the threshold in its first season and must register no later than the end of the following calendar month/quarter; if services are performed by a non-resident without a permanent establishment and total revenues remain below C$30,000, registration is optional but is recommended to claim input tax credit refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or invoice-by-invoice API mandate exists under the Excise Tax Act; CRA accepts GST/HST returns through NETFILE and B2B/EDI gateways but does not validate individual invoices in real time. Quebec, however, has enacted a phased mandatory electronic-invoicing and e-reporting obligation under the Tax Administration Act (CQLR c. A-6.002): large enterprises must issue PEPPOL-compliant structured e-invoices (Factur-X or UBL) from January 1, 2026, with medium and small enterprises brought in progressively by 2029. Until the applicable phase-in date, paper or generic PDF invoices bearing the GST/HST and QST registration numbers, supplier name, client name, description of the marine survey services, and tax amounts remain legally compliant for deduction and zero-rating documentation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A marine insurance surveyor may claim zero-rating on two alternative statutory bases. First, a supply of an inspection, testing, or evaluating service in respect of tangible personal property that is exported by the recipient is zero-rated where the goods are exported from Canada no later than the 60th day after the service is fully performed, the exporter is the recipient or related person, and the supplier obtains the prescribed export evidence within the document-retention window. Second, a supply of a surveying or claims-advisory service to a non-resident underwriter may be zero-rated where the non-resident is not registered and does not carry on business in Canada and the service does not relate to tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed; an on-site hull or cargo survey at a Quebec port therefore cannot qualify under the second rule, and the surveyor must instead rely on the export-of-goods rule if the damaged cargo or vessel is subsequently exported. Desk-based claims review, loss-ratio analysis, and survey report preparation performed wholly outside Canada are zero-rated as non-resident services. QST zero-rating mirrors the federal test; where zero-rating applies, the LP retains full input tax credit entitlement and may claim a refund of Quebec input tax refunds in respect of the exported supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A or CBSA electronic export report)
Bill of Lading (port-to-port or multimodal, identifying the insured cargo and consignee)
Inward Remittance Certificate (correspondent-bank SWIFT credit advice evidencing foreign-currency receipt of the survey fee)
Cargo or Hull Damage Survey Report (dated, showing vessel IMO number, survey location, and damaged property description)
Underwriter claim settlement voucher or foreign-cargo policy endorsement sheet linking the survey fee to the insured claim
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Quebec perform targeted export-verification audits of zero-rated professional fees because marine surveys are frequently performed at the border and the export evidence is often late or internally inconsistent. The standard assessment window is four years; it extends to seven years for careless or misleading statements and is unlimited for fraudulent misrepresentation. Civil penalties include a 25% gross-negligence penalty on the net tax understated, a default penalty of 5% plus 1%-2% monthly for unreported GST/QST, and Quebec administrative penalties under the Tax Administration Act of up to 25% of the amount misreported. Retrospective clawbacks are common: if the prescribed export documentation is not retained for six years, the authorities reverse the zero-rating, assess GST/QST at 14.975% on the full survey fee, deny the corresponding input tax credits, and charge interest compounded daily. Criminal liability arises under the Excise Tax Act where export invoices are fabricated or grossly inflated, with fines on conviction, imprisonment, and publication of the taxpayer's name in the federal and Quebec tax registries.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), Ottawa, acting in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as banking regulator and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the AML supervisory authority. Canada operates a market-determined freely floating exchange rate regime; there is no foreign exchange control act, no central-bank approval desk for commercial transactions, and no exchange control quota or licensing system applicable to current or capital account operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full legal convertibility of the Canadian dollar (CAD) for both current account and capital account transactions under the Currency Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. C-52), the Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. B-2) and Canada's IMF Article VIII obligations. Profit remittance, partnership distributions, dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, capital repatriation and liquidation proceeds may be paid to non-residents without prior regulatory consent. The practical hurdles are limited to: (i) Investment Canada Act net-benefit review for non-controlling or above-threshold controlling acquisitions (this marine surveying business, classified under ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390, falls below the WTO-increased threshold and is not a Cultural Business); (ii) Part XIII Canadian withholding tax, treaty-reduced where applicable, on passive distributions to foreign partners; (iii) Quebec registration obligations under the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and the French-language business rules of the Charte de la langue française; and (iv) statutory reporting under the Income Tax Act, including Form T1135 when the cost amount of foreign property held by a Canadian tax resident partner exceeds CAD 100,000. Service fees and claim-settlement monies are freely receivable and convertible in either CAD or foreign currency at market rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts or service fee revenue, including marine survey fees earned from non-resident underwriters. Exporters may retain foreign currency indefinitely in Canadian Foreign Currency Accounts or offshore bank accounts. The only compliance obligations are informational: (i) Canada Border Services Agency export declarations where goods accompany or are embedded in the surveying engagement; (ii) FINTRAC's International Electronic Funds Transfer Report obligation imposed on the financial institution for every cross-border wire of CAD 10,000 or more, with no requirement that funds be brought onshore; and (iii) the T1135 foreign-property reporting threshold applicable to resident partners, which is an income-tax reporting duty, not a currency-restoration duty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Trust Deposit Account (CDN and USD) and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with USD clearing sub-account
Operational Account with USD clearing sub-account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational disbursement rails and Low for escrow or fiduciary functions. A FINTRAC-registered Money Service Business operating in Canada, including Wise acting through its Canadian MSB registration, may lawfully execute low-value cross-border vendor wires, expense reimbursements and foreign-currency payouts for the LP. However, an offshore EMI that is not registered as an MSB with FINTRAC cannot hold a CAD settlement account, cannot clear through Payments Canada rails, and will not satisfy the compliance standard for escrowed third-party funds. Where the marine surveying contract requires the LP to receive underwriter claim monies and disburse them to repairers or adjusters, those funds must be held in a Canadian Schedule I bank or regulated trust company and must never be commingled in an EMI omnibus wallet. Recommended protocol: deploy Wise only for operational disbursements below the governing partnership agreement's materiality threshold and route all capital injections and escrowed claim settlements through a tier-1 Canadian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person or verifiable live-video identity verification is required for at least one designated signatory of the General Partner; fully remote account opening without interview is not available for non-resident participants. FINTRAC's prescribed client-identification methods permit video-conference verification using two original government-issued photo documents, but Canadian Schedule I banks internally overlaid a mandatory branch-meeting or notarized-identity-certification step for limited partnerships. National Bank of Canada, RBC and TD will typically require either (i) attendance of a General Partner principal at a Canadian branch with corporate seals and the Registraire des entreprises extract, or (ii) a scheduled video interview with an account manager during which the identification documents are shown live. For a Quebec LP with non-resident limited partners, banks require the deposit of the certified copy of the LP agreement and a notarized certificate of incumbency for the General Partner; remote-only opening is denied where any beneficial owner is domiciled in a FATF-listed or sanctions-affected jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity inherent in the Limited Partnership vehicle, triggering enhanced customer due diligence and the statutory 25% ultimate-beneficial-owner identification threshold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered extract from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ), the executed LP Agreement, General Partner certificate of incumbency, an organization chart identifying every partner holding 25% or more of the capital or profits, notarized passport copies and residential-address proof for all such ultimate beneficial owners, plus a signed undertaking to report any UBO change within the bank's required notice period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injections from non-resident partners and underwriter-sourced funds, raising source-of-funds, sanctions and politically-exposed-person concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital subscription agreements and the LP Agreement amendment authorizing the capital call, a six-month bank reference letter from the remitting foreign institution, a source-of-wealth statement for each contributing partner, negative media and sanctions/PEP self-certifications, and complete FATCA/CRS tax forms including IRS Form W-8BEN-E or W-9 and the Canada CRS self-certification for any US participating partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering indicator: recurring fee income from non-resident marine insurers or underwriters for survey services, flagged as cash-flow mismatch or over/under-invoicing in the ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390 segment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid statutory licence or registration with the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) and current professional-liability insurance, executed marine survey service agreements with named underwriters, itemized invoices with a clear fee schedule and stated CAD or USD currency terms, retained technical survey and inspection reports for each engagement, and a written business narrative explaining the claims-loss-adjustment and fee-disbursement model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large-value and high-frequency cross-border wires that meet FINTRAC's CAD 10,000 International Electronic Funds Transfer Report threshold or a substantial mismatch between the LP's declared activity and its expected transaction profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-approved treasury mandate covering expected wire frequency, counterparties and value bands, complete beneficial-ownership schedule, ISO 20022/SWIFT purpose codes for each remittance, original invoices, claim files and disbursement schedules establishing that every transfer relates to survey fees or escrowed claim settlements rather than concealed lending or conversion of criminal proceeds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound partner capital contributions must be transmitted as SWIFT MT103 messages (or ISO 20022 pacs.008 equivalents) carrying the ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' or the narrative 'Capital contribution — Quebec Limited Partnership', and must reference the LP's NEQ registration number and the corresponding capital-call letter. Settlement occurs through the receiving Canadian bank's LVTS or ACSS clearing infrastructure into a dedicated CAD, USD, or foreign-currency operational/escrow account depending on the LP Agreement's currency clauses. The remitting bank will generate FINTRAC reporting automatically where the wire equals or exceeds CAD 10,000, and the receiving bank must reconcile source-of-funds documentation against the capital-call schedule. For USD injections, best practice is to route via the Canadian bank's US clearing node (Fedwire or CHIPS) and then perform an internal ledger transfer into the LP's USD sub-account, thereby avoiding unnecessary FX spreads; the bank will apply its published corporate FX rate only when the partner instructs conversion into CAD.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements and claim disbursements flow through two primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 international payments for vendor, adjuster and repairer wires, and (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit issued, advised or confirmed by a Canadian Schedule I bank under UCP600 for large documentary claim settlements or recurring supply arrangements. The CAD legs clear through Payments Canada's ACSS or LVTS, while USD legs clear via Fedwire or CHIPS through the bank's US correspondent or wholly owned US banking entity. Every disbursement instruction must identify the beneficiary's legal name, full address, BIC and account number, and must carry a purpose narrative referencing the claim-file number and underlying survey report. For escrowed claim funds, dual-signature authorization by two General Partner principals is mandatory, and no settlement may be executed against an EMI wallet except for de minimis operational vendor payments expressly authorized in the treasury mandate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable outright foreign-exchange forwards with tenors up to 24 months, freely available from Canadian Schedule I banks without underlying trade documentation verification because Canada imposes no exchange-control requirement
CAD/USD foreign-exchange swaps combining spot and forward legs for aligning contribution-date and distribution-date liquidity
Cross-currency swaps (cross-currency interest rate swaps) for longer-dated CAD/USD capital-commitment and distribution-hedging structures
CAD/USD over-the-counter foreign-exchange options documented under ISDA or IFEMA master agreements with a Canadian Schedule I bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration (déclaration annuelle) confirming registered details of the Quebec limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be filed no later than the anniversary date of the partnership's initial registration each year; the filing window opens 60 days before the anniversary date and closes at 11:59:59 p.m. on the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a CAD 6 fixed penalty and additional late-filing costs; continued failure to file beyond the required annual cycle may result in a notice of default and, if unremedied, administrative dissolution and strike-off of the partnership registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and partnership schedules covering the fiscal period ended in the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal period end; for a December 31 fiscal period, the filing deadline is May 31 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late-filing penalty applies under Income Tax Act section 162(7.1) at CAD 25 per partner per day, subject to a minimum of CAD 100 and a maximum of CAD 2,500; interest accrues on any unpaid amounts and gross negligence penalties may apply in cases of knowing omission.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is imposed on an ordinary private Quebec limited partnership by provincial legislation. An audit becomes compulsory only if the partnership agreement or unanimous partner agreement requires it, a court or arbitrator so orders on application by a partner or creditor, the partnership is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities laws, or a professional licensing scheme relevant to marine survey services mandates audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: A non-public Quebec limited partnership generally prepares financial statements in accordance with Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) may also be adopted. Where the partnership is part of a public reporting group or required to file with a securities regulator, IFRS applies. The Civil Code of Quebec and the partnership agreement also require books and records sufficient to determine contributions, profits, losses, distributions and partners' entitlements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual declaration to the Registraire des entreprises must confirm each general partner's name and identifying information and any ultimate beneficial natural person exercising a 25% or greater ownership or control interest in the limited partnership. A transfer of limited partnership units is not filed with the registrar at the time of transfer; it is recorded in the internal register of partners, and the revised ownership percentages and ultimate beneficial owner details are confirmed in the next annual declaration. All such changes must also be documented in the partnership minute book and reported to Revenu Québec as part of the annual filing if the partnership has a Quebec establishment.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners' Units and Ownership Interests
Register of General Partners' Resolutions and Consents
Minute Book containing the partnership agreement, capital call records, waivers and indemnity authorizations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 300 – CAD 1,500 per annum (approx. USD 220 – USD 1,100) for a registered office, registered agent and entity maintenance service in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 6,500 for an independent audit of a small to mid-sized marine insurance surveying limited partnership if required by the partnership agreement, a lender, or a client contract

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined 26.5% (Canada federal 15% + Quebec provincial 11.5%) for corporate partners; the Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and pays no entity-level corporate income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to a Quebec LP. Corporate partners that are Canadian-controlled private corporations may reduce their effective rate via the federal Small Business Deduction (9% federal rate) and the Quebec reduced rate (3% on active business income up to CAD 500,000), as well as SR&ED investment tax credits for qualifying marine survey and engineering R&D. The LP itself does not claim these incentives; they flow to partners.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 – Partnership Information Return (Canada); filed via CRA My Business Account, CRA T5013 Web Forms, or EDI-approved tax preparation software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within five months after the partnership's fiscal period end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name, Business Number, jurisdiction of formation (Quebec LP), address of principal place of business, fiscal year-end, legal entity type code, and relevant marine claims surveying business or professional license identifiers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Canadian permanent establishment address and indicate that the partnership maintains a place of business in Quebec. Provide foreign registration details of the general partner if located outside Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B – Statement of Partnership Income / Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from vessel hull and cargo damage claim inspection surveys (ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390), cost of sales, operating expenses, and net income or loss on a commercial basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source revenue attributable to services performed in Canada or from a Canadian permanent establishment. Do not include foreign survey fees unless they are part of the Canadian business operations; apply treaty business-profit allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of net income/loss among partners by percentage and by province of residence. Quebec and federal allocation is based on the location of the permanent establishment and where services were rendered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, report the share of income taxable in Canada under Part I and, if the partner is a resident of a treaty country, address whether the permanent establishment threshold is met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of T5013 incurs a penalty of CAD $25 per day for each return, up to CAD $2,500. If the failure is knowingly committed, an additional penalty of the greater of CAD $100 and 50% of the tax that was required to be deducted or withheld may be assessed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 – Declaration de renseignements des sociétés de personnes / Partnership Information Return for Quebec; filed via Revenu Québec's Mon compte d'entreprise (CLIC) portal. The related RL-15 slips are issued to partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CO-17 must be filed within six months after the partnership's fiscal period end. RL-15 slips must be issued and transmitted to Revenu Québec by the last day of February following the calendar year in which the fiscal period ends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), legal form (Limited Partnership), address of the partnership's establishment, date of registration, and name of the general partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the non-resident status of each general and limited partner. Include a foreign address and the partner's country of residence; confirm the partnership's place of management and Quebec permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part B – Determinants of Income / Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec-source income/loss derived from surveying activities (including ship hull and cargo claim inspections), expenses incurred in Quebec, and the partnership's taxable income attributable to Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to Quebec based on the proportion of wages and revenues in Quebec; exclude income from contracts performed entirely outside Canada, except where overlapping with a permanent establishment. For non-resident partners, the Quebec allocation follows the federal allocation unless modified by the Quebec Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part C – Partner Information and Slips
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, addresses, residency, share percentages, and allocated income/loss for each partner. Production of RL-15 slips must match the CO-17 totals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, identify their country of residence and treaty position. Do not issue RL-15 if the income is exempt from Part XIII withholding; provide an explanation of the treaty basis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Quebec late-filing penalty is CAD $25 per day for each required return, up to CAD $2,500. For a failure exceeding 60 days, an additional penalty equal to 5% of the amount owing plus 1% per month of active tax liability can be levied. Willful negligence carries fines and imprisonment under the Quebec Tax Administration Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T106 – Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Resident Persons; filed via CRA electronic T106 system or paper form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the same date as the T5013 (five months after fiscal year-end; March 31 for December 31 year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part I – Transaction and Party Identification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List each non-resident related party, the relationship, nature of the transactions (e.g., management fees, intercompany survey fees, insurance claim advancement), currency, and the aggregate fair market value.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If total reportable transactions with a single non-resident related party exceed CAD $1 million, the T106 is mandatory. For non-resident partners or affiliates, state the transfer pricing method chosen and the functional/risk profile of each entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide the arm's length price, the methodology selected (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, profit split), and the comparability adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled transactions must be supported by contemporaneous documentation; penalty relief may be available when reasonable documentation was prepared. Note any cross-border apportionment of profits from worldwide survey services.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete T106 is penalized at CAD $100 per filing per day, to a maximum of CAD $2,500. Deficiencies in transfer pricing documentation may trigger an additional 10% penalty on the net upward adjustment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Canada's statutory Part XIII withholding tax rate is 25% for dividends paid by a Canadian corporation. A Limited Partnership, being fiscally transparent, does not pay dividends to partners; distributions are not subject to dividend withholding tax. Allocated taxable income is instead reported on each partner's return (T1/T2) and taxed according to the partner's status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident claiming reduced or zero Canadian withholding treaty benefits must file the relevant CRA forms before or with the tax return: submit a completed Form NR301 (or the equivalent provincial form) together with a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the home country tax authority; reference the applicable treaty article and provide factual evidence of the absence of a Canadian permanent establishment. For partnership distributions, no withholding return is made. For dividend, interest or royalty payments, use Forms NR301 and NR302 and submit before the payment to avoid gross-basis withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate for interest, royalties (including IP rents) and certain trust payments is 25% when paid to a non-arm's length non-resident. Under Canada's treaties, the rate on interest is usually 15% (0% or 10% for arm's length or certain long-term interest), and royalties commonly 10%–15% depending on the treaty and type of arrangement. Quebec does not levy a second-level WHT on LP payments; the federal tax is administered by CRA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD $1 million in aggregate fair market value of reportable cross-border transactions with a single non-resident related party triggers mandatory T106 and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File). A Country-by-Country Report is required for groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or CAD equivalent.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada and Quebec do not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulations code. The federal General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s.245) and Quebec GAAR (Tax Administration Act s.1079.4) deny tax benefits arising from arrangements lacking true economic substance, commercial purpose, or that rely on artificial steps. In an LP context, the general partner must demonstrate actual managerial capacity, premises, and operational activity in Quebec; a pure shell partnership with non-resident partners may be challenged and recharacterized.
